tagline: The Pacific kingdom that stayed a kingdom
overview:
Tonga is a Polynesian country of about 170 islands in the South Pacific, of which around 36 are inhabited. They are scattered in a long north-south chain east of Fiji, and their combined land area is only about 747 km², smaller than New York City, though they are spread across a huge stretch of ocean.

About 105,000 people live in Tonga, speaking Tongan and English. Nuku'alofa, the capital, is on Tongatapu, the largest and flattest island, where most of the population lives.

Tonga is a constitutional monarchy, and it is the only Pacific island nation that was never fully colonized by a foreign power, keeping its royal line unbroken for around a thousand years. Farming, fishing, tourism and money sent home by Tongans living in New Zealand, Australia and the United States support the economy. Rugby is close to a national religion, and Tongan players appear on teams worldwide.
landAndNature: Tonga's islands come in two kinds: low coral islands in the east, including flat Tongatapu ringed by reef, and steep volcanic islands to the west, some still active. The country sits beside the Tonga Trench, one of the deepest places in any ocean at over 10,800 meters. In January 2022 the undersea volcano Hunga Tonga-Hunga Ha'apai exploded in one of the most powerful eruptions ever recorded, sending a plume into space, triggering tsunami waves and being heard as far away as Alaska. Humpback whales come from Antarctica each winter to give birth in the warm, sheltered water, and Tonga is one of the few places where people may swim with them. Flying foxes, large fruit bats, hang in protected trees at Kolovai.
peopleAndCulture: Tongan life places family, church and respect for rank at the center. Sunday is quiet by law: shops close, and most people attend church, where hymn singing in rich harmony fills the buildings. The ta'ovala, a woven pandanus mat worn wrapped around the waist over clothes, is formal dress for school, work and ceremonies. Ngatu, or tapa cloth, is beaten from mulberry bark by groups of women and painted with brown patterns, then given in enormous lengths at weddings and funerals. Feasts are laid on long low tables with roast pig, root crops and coconut cream dishes cooked in an umu oven. Rugby union is the favorite sport, and the national team performs the sipi tau challenge before matches.
history: Lapita voyagers settled Tonga around 2,800 years ago, and from about 950 the Tu'i Tonga line of kings built an empire whose influence reached Fiji, Samoa and beyond; huge stone tombs and the coral trilithon Ha'amonga 'a Maui date from that era. Dutch sailors arrived in the 1600s and James Cook in the 1770s, calling the islands the Friendly Islands. Missionaries brought Christianity in the 1800s, and King George Tupou I united the islands, freed commoners from serfdom and gave Tonga a constitution in 1875. Tonga accepted British protection in 1900 while keeping its own monarchy and government, and full control of foreign affairs returned in 1970. Reform movements led to a more democratic parliament in 2010, with most seats now elected by the people.
funFacts: Tonga is one of the first places on Earth to see each new day, thanks to its position near the date line.
The 2022 eruption of Hunga Tonga sent a plume higher than any volcanic cloud ever measured, reaching the edge of space.
Tonga's constitution makes Sunday a day of rest, and even most shops and flights pause.
Tonga has never been ruled by a foreign power and keeps a royal line stretching back around a thousand years.
Tongan tapa cloth is sometimes made in single pieces tens of meters long for weddings and royal occasions.
